shard: Spain and Portugal: every pending row of scripts/data/rosterConfirmation2026.json whose club plays in La Liga or the Primeira Liga as Club Manager models them for 2026-27 (48 rows at origin/main 5f2622fd: Spain 31, Portugal 17)
method: Each row was read on the web on 2026-10-03, never a wiki. Most pages were read with WebFetch and WebSearch; where WebFetch could not render a page or summarised it poorly, the raw page or the public JSON behind it was fetched from the shell with curl or a small node script and read directly (ESPN squad pages for several seasons, the Eredivisie's Feyenoord page, the Braga, Porto, Vitória and Tondela sites, Liga Portugal's public player records at www.ligaportugal.pt/bo/api/players and Vitória's own player records). A source fetched that way is the same publisher's page as its url says, read as text rather than through a summary. A row leaves pending only when an official page (family A: the LaLiga player or match page, the Liga Portugal page, a club's own squad page or announcement, or a governing body such as the AFC) and an independent publisher on another host (family B: Soccerway, FotMob, ESPN) agree where the man is. Birth dates are in the note so a namesake cannot be mistaken for him. A season-long loanee is placed at the club he plays for, with loan and loanFrom as information only, the ledger's loanPolicy. The to field is the Club Manager club name the bake knows; realClub is the club as the sources write it. This file is folded into rosterConfirmation2026.json by the lead; nothing reads it directly.
forTheFold: 30 of the 48 rows are settled on both families; 18 stay pending, each with its reason and what was tried. Read before folding: (1) The web search budget of the session ran out early in this shard, so every row after Benfica was read only through pages reached directly or by following links (ESPN squad and player pages, LaLiga player and match pages, club and league pages). That is why the pending list is long, not because the evidence points the other way. (2) Spain settled well: LaLiga's player and match pages answered for 29 of 31 Spanish rows. Portugal did not: Porto, Braga, Vitória, Famalicão, Estrela and Liga Portugal all render their squads in script, and Liga Portugal's public player records (www.ligaportugal.pt/bo/api/players) carry name, birth date and shirt number but no club. Benfica's and Sporting's own squad pages did answer. So five Portuguese rows (Cláudio Ramos, Vasco Sousa, Diego Rodrigues, Gustavo Silva, Toni Borevković) are pending on one family only: ESPN's 2026-27 page and the league's shirt number both put each man where the game already has him, so leaving them pending changes nothing in game. The exception is Borevković: ESPN's player page also lists him starting three Süper Lig games for Samsunspor (modelled) in August 2026 before two Vitória games in September, and nothing read explains it, so his row is not a plain one family short case. (3) Eight pending rows are not at the from club on every source read, only the destination is unsettled: Renato Sanches (not on Benfica's or PSG's 2026-27 pages), Tiago Gouveia (ESPN: Gençlerbirliği, modelled), Brian Oliván, Agustín Álvarez, Clément Michelin, André Horta, Kaio César (ESPN: Corinthians, modelled) and Tiago Silva. For Oliván, Álvarez, Michelin, Horta and Tiago Silva every candidate club read is unmodelled, but only two of them have an official page behind them. Michelin and Horta: LaLiga's own player page puts each at an unmodelled club (Real Valladolid, Almería) and ESPN leaves each out of his from club, so both families agree he has left; the lead may remove those two now and record the club later. Oliván, Álvarez and Tiago Silva rest on ESPN alone (and Talleres' own squad page does not list Álvarez), so removing them now would skip the rule that both families agree; they wait for an official page. Gouveia, Kaio César and Rafa Soares (ESPN: Estrela Amadora, modelled) would be moves if an official page agrees. (4) Namesakes: LaLiga's page under the slug gerard-moreno is a goalkeeper born 2005 at Sporting Gijón, not Villarreal's Gerard Moreno (born 1992), and was not used; Youssef Enríquez is the man LaLiga files under youssef-lekhedim and ESPN lists as Youssef Lekhedim (same shirt 3, same birth date 2005-10-07); Vasco Sousa has a namesake league record (a defender born 2004). (5) Every to field is a Club Manager club name (Getafe, FC Copenhagen, Rayo Vallecano, Levante, Mainz, Real Betis, Feyenoord twice), and every removed row's club is in no modelled league. Lekue is notCurrent because he retired; the Athletic Club announcement page refuses WebFetch (HTTP 403), so its title was read from the search index and FotMob, El Gol Digital and the 2026-27 LaLiga and ESPN squads carry the rest. (6) A convention for the lead to rule on across shards: two removals here rest on an official page that proves only an absence. Ángel Correa: Liga MX's Tigres page shows he is not at Tigres, and no official Atlético or River Plate page could be read. Hugo Félix: Benfica's page shows he is not at Benfica, and Tondela's site renders its squad in script. Both destinations are on two independent publishers (Soccerway with FotMob or EFE). That is weaker than the rule that both families agree where the man is; Germany's shard (Round 930) has a similar row (Joel Vega Zambrano). Either keep such rows as removals, since no source read puts the man at his from club and every destination read is unmodelled, or move them to pending until an official destination page is read.
